name_reason: Follows the fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (gfx/screen domain) and accurately reflects the purpose: restore a previously saved screen block from its backup buffer (the inverse of fd2_save_screen_block_to_buffer). No Ghidra address residue in the name; all suffix tokens are descriptive words, not hex addresses.
purpose: Outer setter for a screen-block restore: seeds the width/height blit-state globals from the saved-block buffer header, resolves the destination pointer, and hands off to the inner copy loop that repaints the saved pixels.
logic_summary: Reads the saved-block header at saved_block: word0 -> data_fd2_graphics_rle_blit_cur_width (0x627B4, width), word2 -> data_fd2_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows (0x627B6, height). Computes restore_dst = dst + *(uint32*)(saved_block+4) (the dst_offset to the region top-left) and src = saved_block+8 (start of the contiguous saved pixels). Calls fd2_restore_block_loop(restore_dst, src, stride) which does the per-row REP MOVSB copy. In the binary the whole body is wrapped in PUSHAD/POPAD and ends with a plain RET (cdecl); the inner loop receives src/dst/stride via registers (ESI walked to saved_block+8 by 2 LODSW + 1 LODSD, EDI=resolved dst, EBP=stride). EAX is preserved by POPAD, so the decompiler's 'return in_EAX' is a pass-through artifact and the sole caller discards it -> effectively void.
signature: void __cdecl fd2_restore_screen_block_from_buffer(uint32 saved_block, uint32 dst, uint32 stride)

params.name: saved_block
params.semantics: Pointer to the saved-block backup buffer header: [+0] uint16 width, [+2] uint16 height, [+4] uint32 dst_offset, [+8] width*height contiguous saved pixel bytes. Built by the save companion fd2_save_screen_block_to_buffer; the caller passes the malloc'd 'save under' buffer.
params.reason: Descriptive and matches caller usage (the save-under buffer) and body usage (header read at +0/+2/+4, pixels at +8). No address residue.

params.name: dst
params.semantics: Destination base linear address; the region top-left is reached by adding the header's dst_offset (saved_block+4).
params.reason: Standard descriptor for the destination base; matches the caller's dst arg and the body's EDI = dst + dst_offset. No address residue.

params.name: stride
params.semantics: Bytes to advance the destination per row; forwarded to the inner copy loop as the row stride (EBP).
params.reason: Accurate descriptor for the per-row destination advance; matches the caller's dst_pitch arg and the body's EBP load. No address residue.

returns.semantics: Void. The binary preserves EAX via POPAD; the decompiler's 'return in_EAX' is a pass-through artifact, and the sole caller (fd2_cleanup_dialog_sprite_buffer) discards any value.

notes: Source definition (blitspr.c lines 1744-1755) and its comment block (1702-1743) are accurate, precise, ASCII, and match the disassembly at 0x4E92C exactly; comment kept as-is. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with the refined understanding (same buffer layout, body, register passing, and void-return artifact), so plate left untouched. Globals written: 0x627B4 (cur_width), 0x627B6 (remaining_rows), both written then read by the inner loop fd2_restore_block_loop @ 0x4E954; not added to reads_globals since this function only writes them. Sole caller fd2_cleanup_dialog_sprite_buffer @ 0x15E71 confirms the three-param semantics (sprite_buf, dst, dst_pitch).
